key_concepts: Gravity keeps the Sun, Moon, and Earth moving in the solar system
Earth rotates on its axis and revolves around the Sun
Earth's rotation causes daytime and nighttime
Moon phases result from the changing visible portion of the Moon's sunlit side
A new moon occurs when the Moon is between the Sun and Earth
A full moon occurs when Earth is between the Sun and Moon
First and third quarter moons show half of the Moon's illuminated surface from Earth
Waxing phases occur before a full moon and waning phases occur after it
Crescent phases show a small sliver while gibbous phases show more than half illuminated
The Moon's orbit is tilted about five degrees, so eclipses do not occur every month
Solar eclipses occur when the Moon lines up directly with the Sun
